inspiration.observed_pattern: A joined pre-membership purchase CTE assigns DENSE_RANK by descending purchase date, then the outer grouped query keeps the latest rank and concatenates all tied product labels.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a membership purchase summary with independently named tables, explicit tie ordering inside GROUP_CONCAT, an excluded post-membership purchase, and customers without qualifying purchases omitted. The source rank typo is corrected to the CTE alias used by the outer filter.

fixture_notes: Customer 41 has two purchases tied on the latest pre-membership date and both labels must survive; customer 42 has one qualifying purchase; customer 43 only has a post-membership purchase and is excluded.
determinism_notes: Customer IDs, membership dates, purchase dates, item IDs, rank ordering, concatenation ordering, and final ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE membership_accounts (customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY, member_since DATE NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE purchase_items (purchase_id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT NOT NULL, purchase_date DATE NOT NULL, item_label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH ranked_purchases AS (SELECT p.customer_id, p.purchase_id, p.purchase_date, p.item_label, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.customer_id ORDER BY p.purchase_date DESC) AS purchase_rank FROM purchase_items AS p INNER JOIN membership_accounts AS m ON m.customer_id = p.customer_id WHERE p.purchase_date < m.member_since) SELECT customer_id, GROUP_CONCAT(item_label ORDER BY purchase_date DESC, purchase_id SEPARATOR '|') AS latest_items FROM ranked_purchases WHERE purchase_rank = 1 GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY customer_id

checks.sql: SELECT purchase_id, customer_id, purchase_date, item_label FROM purchase_items ORDER BY purchase_id
